facts.text: Camp Hale sits at 9,238 feet, chosen for its high altitude and abundant snowfall, making it ideal for mountain warfare training.
Named after General Irving Hale, the camp’s title honors the officer who pioneered U.S. mountain warfare tactics.
During World War II, the 10th Mountain Division trained here in alpine climbing, skiing, and cold‑weather survival before heading to Europe.
Hollywood filmed two wartime movies at Camp Hale—"Mountain Fighters" (1943) and "I Love a Soldier" (1944)—capturing the camp’s rugged scenery.
In 1992, Camp Hale became a national historic site, and in 2019 it was proposed as Colorado’s first National Historic Landscape under the CORE Act.
Veteran Pete Seibert, who trained at Camp Hale, founded Vail Ski Resort in 1962, turning the area into a world‑class ski destination.
